Salesman covered everything and answered all of my millions of questions.Installation was quick and efficient with polite, respectful workers.Had a few issues getting the Enphase system to report properly with our two phase meter system, but the electricians came back promptly and sorted the problem.

The sales team had a good understanding of my solar requirements and went the extra mile to offer solutions to my problems. The team is honest and checks with the client after installation to ensure that everything went okay. Questions and issues were resolved ASAP where possible.

We recently engaged SOLARLAB in Adelaide to install our new solar system.  The final system design ended up with 22 Hyundai 390W shingled panels and Enphase IQ7+ microinverters, the Envoy-S along with a Telsa PowerWall.We don't have a north facing roof, and some of our panels had to face east (approx azimuth 131 degrees), bulk of them to the west (approx azimuth 312 degrees), and a little bit of shading in the late afternoon on some of the west facing panels.  We all agreed that the micro inverter option would most likely provide us with the best result, along with our desire to avoid the high voltage DC in the roof from a string setup.  To support the bulk of the electrical loads in the house from a blackout and provide possible future support for an electric vehicle, we also went ahead with a Tesla PowerWall battery unit.The whole engagement, from the first sales visit, right through to the installation and commissioning of the system was great.  All of the SOLARLAB staff were very friendly and nothing was too much trouble.  There were no pushy sales tactics, and they were willing to discuss different designs and what the benefits of each were.  Most other companies just seemed to install a simple string setup to keep the price down, maybe thinking the lowest price wins.Once the install was finished, a small issue with the Envoy-S incorrectly limiting the exported power was resolved quickly without any fuss or drama.  At one time or another we spoke with everyone from the CEO through to the guys fixing the racking and panels to the roof, everyone was great to work with.One of the things that we really liked about SOLARLAB is that they have their own people to do all of the work, they don't contract the work out to other companies.  We think this gives a more consistent result on the installations and the care that goes into the job certainly shows.We are really happy with the finished system, and considering the alignment of the panels because of our roof layout, the system still generates an impressive amount of power.  On most days so far, we have not had to draw any power from the grid (other than the few really hot days in Feb when we had to run our A/C, which is a big unit) and have exported anything up to 42kWh of power to the grid, after charging the PowerWall up and satisfying the needs of the house during the day.  The PowerWall typically discharges down to around 83% capacity overnight after running a TV, the fridge, some inside lighting (now all LED) and a porch light at the front of the house.  It is normally fully charged by 10:30am and ready to go for the next night's requirements.SOLARLAB organised all of the approvals, assisted with a "green" finance package with one of their partners, guided us through the Home Battery scheme sign up that we have here in SA which provides a State Government backed subsidy for home battery storage and even booked the smart meter replacement with our electricity retailer.As with any solar system, to get the best of it you need to adjust when you use most of your electricity.  The SolarQuotes team has provided advice on this on the website, and it is amazing what a few small changes to your consumption habits can make.  After only a few weeks from the installation and by using the stats from the Tesla and Enphase apps it has been really easy to make these small changes.If you are located in South Australia, we would highly recommend including SOLARLAB on your list of companies to talk to about a solar system.

Once deciding to go ahead with solar (and very thankful we did!) we obtained three quotes through solar quotes, but I also used the solar quotes website to select three other installers in the Adelaide area.  Over two weeks, six companies came to my home to quote and recommend systems.  I have a curved roof and I insisted to each company that they should view my site prior to quoting.  I received multiple quotes from each installer, which allowed me to select the system best suited to my current (DC in this case!) and future energy needs.  We plan to purchase an electric vehicle in the next 1-2 years, so we picked the biggest recommended single phase system we could afford.  We chose Solarlab because they were really good at customer service and Justin was always quick to respond to my many emails, texts and phone calls.  On the day of the installation, the crew commenced before at 8am and had completely finished by 5pm that day and the site was left clean and tidy.  I was able to see the benefits of my system through live monitoring the next day and have become an information geek when it comes to PV systems. Using my solar power daily is the way to go!

Initial contact was pleasant, with the quotes being detailed enough yet not overwhelming, which made the comparison with other quotes easy. There was a small miscommunication over the first on-site inspection by the installer, but that was quickly cleared up, and the installer (Max) and his team subsequently did a fantastic job. Quick and efficient installation under changing weather conditions, well done. The panels and inverter are good quality so far, so we're happy. Our only small criticism would be the Fronius app to allow us to view continuous performance of the system, which took some time, effort and a small amount of frustration to set up, but that's not entirely the fault of the installation company.

Our experience with SOLARLAB was exceptional from the on-site meeting with Steve Byerlee, through his configuration option presentation and selection, and to the installation itself. This was tarnished by administration issues: (1) an unexplained rejection of financing from their preferred financing partner; (2) not receiving an adjusted invoice to reflect financing was no longer being used; and (3) challenges with splitting payment between bank transfer and credit card. Those issues aside, I would be seeking SOLARLAB again if needed.

Having access to both the Telsa app and Enphase app has been fantastic to be able to see both a system summary and panel-by-panel performance insight.Lucas was really helpful during the whole process and the installation team where kind and considerate. The electricians were a stand-out, doing a clean, neat and tidy install of all the components and answering my curiosity questions as they were finishing up.I have started to recommend the team to family, friends and work colleagues - really impressed.Thanks guys.
